# Findings

## The CI merge-tree index gate races with generated files edited on both sides

- **Signature:** merge-tree-index-generated-file-race
- **Evidence:** PR #1566 red four times at qa-validate's "OpenSpec index on the merge tree" step (runs `45353115231`, `45382025221`, `45394053201`, and the run before the #1493 findings gate) with first error `[merge-tree-index] MERGE CONFLICT: rebase on current master and retry`. Each time the head was rebased onto the fetched tip and both generated files regenerated (`make openspec-index`, `make architecture-refresh`), the local simulation of the exact step was rc=0, and a master commit landed during the ~15-minute `validate` job editing the same generated files (`553e4bfb`, `6e50fc25`, `972f8261`, `e84439bf` all touch `OPENSPEC.md`; `972f8261` also touches `ARCHITECTURE.md`). Local `git merge --no-commit --no-ff origin/master` against the newer tip reproduced `CONFLICT (content): ARCHITECTURE.md` and `OPENSPEC.md` every time.
- **Why:** a PR that archives its OpenSpec change must edit the generated index and inventory, and any master merge that archives another change edits the same count lines. The gate refuses the textual conflict instead of evaluating the merge tree's generated artifacts, so a correct head goes red through no fault of its own and every re-push starts another 15-minute race.
- **Done when:** the merge-tree step regenerates `OPENSPEC.md` (and the `ARCHITECTURE.md` inventory block) on the merged tree before checking it, or an equivalent deterministic verdict that does not depend on which commit lands while CI runs — with a test that plants a second archive on master mid-run and proves the gate accepts a genuinely current index and still refuses a stale one.

## The host-only exception list has no merge-time defence against master adding a new bare host target

- **Evidence:** master commit `972f8261` (#1563) added the PUBLIC target `pr-draft-check`, which calls `python3 scripts/pr_health.py … --draft-only` on the host (it needs `gh`, absent from the image). The scanner shipped by this PR correctly reded `make lint` on it: `FAIL pr-draft-check (Makefile:652)`. The exception list had to gain a 103rd name on the PR branch before it could go green.
- **Why:** a new host-only seam landing on master while this PR is open is indistinguishable from a new violation, so the guard blocks an unrelated lane's legitimate work until the implementer re-edits the exception list and re-runs a full suite.
- **Done when:** a merge-time reconciliation verifies the exception names against the merged tree's real public targets, or the scanner classifies a `gh`-bound public target by its own command shape so a new host seam cannot silently red the gate.
